u0523.gist: UNEP's 17th Emissions Gap Report, 'The Point of Return' (October 21, 2026), says crossing 1.5°C is now unavoidable; India is the third-largest emitter.
facts: Global emissions: 58.4 GtCO2e in 2025 vs a revised 58.5 GtCO2e in 2024; no confirmed peak.
Cuts needed from 2025 levels: 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040.
Full NDC implementation gives only 5–8% cuts by 2030 and 11–15% by 2035.
India: 4.5 billion tonnes CO2e in 2025, third after China and the United States (excluding LULUCF).
India per person: 3.1 tonnes vs global average 6.4 tonnes; lowest among six largest emitters.
India and China together hold 95% of coal-power capacity under construction worldwide.
u0523.hook: India: third in total (4.5 billion tonnes) but lowest per person (3.1 tonnes): big country, small footprint per head.
u0523.trap: 58.4 Gt = 2025 global emissions; 58.5 Gt = revised 2024 figure. 76% appears twice: G20 share of emissions and share covered by 124 Parties' updated NDCs.

mcq.q: According to UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, what were India's greenhouse gas emissions per person in 2025?
mcq.why: India emitted 3.1 tonnes per person in 2025; the global average was 6.4 tonnes.

mcq.q: Per UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, by how much must global emissions fall by 2035 compared with 2025 levels?
mcq.why: Required cuts from 2025 levels: 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040.

u0524.gist: On October 15, 2026, Sauj Lake (Uttar Pradesh) and Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) became Ramsar Sites, taking India's total to 103.
facts: 103rd: Sauj Lake, Mainpuri district, UP; Ganga floodplain, near Saman Bird Sanctuary.
102nd: Sukhna Wetland, edge of Chandigarh, at the base of the Outer Himalayas.
101st: Glaw Lake (Glaw Tuwi), Lohit district; Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar Site (3 August 2026).
100th: Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal), Ballia, UP (5 June 2026).
Grew from 26 sites (2014) to 103 (2026); India third globally after UK (176) and Mexico (144).
Most sites: Tamil Nadu (20); largest: Sundarbans; smallest: Vembannur; first: Chilika and Keoladeo (1981).
u0524.hook: UP bookends: 100th (Surha Tal, Ballia) and 103rd (Sauj Lake, Mainpuri) are both in Uttar Pradesh.
u0524.trap: Order: Glaw Lake = 101st (Arunachal) → Sukhna = 102nd (Chandigarh) → Sauj Lake = 103rd (UP).
u0524.check: Heading dates Sukhna Wetland 'March 16, 2026', but the text says it was added on October 15, 2026.

mcq.q: Sauj Lake, declared India's 103rd Ramsar Site in October 2026, is in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
mcq.why: Sauj Lake, the 103rd Ramsar Site, is in Mainpuri district of Uttar Pradesh.

mcq.q: Which wetland became Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar Site when announced as India's 101st on 3 August 2026?
mcq.why: Glaw Lake (Glaw Tuwi) in Lohit district was the 101st site and Arunachal's first.

u0525.gist: PM Modi inaugurated India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat, Leh, on October 15, 2026, to protect Ladakh's ancient rock art.
facts: India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park → Sindhu Ghat, Leh (Ladakh).
Inaugurated by PM Modi on October 15, 2026.
Petroglyphs are ancient rock carvings.
The open-air park protects carvings from erosion, infrastructure expansion and unregulated tourism.
u0525.hook: Petro = rock, glyph = carving: petroglyph = rock carving.

mcq.q: Where was India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park inaugurated by PM Modi in October 2026?
mcq.why: PM Modi inaugurated it at Sindhu Ghat in Leh on October 15, 2026.

u0526.gist: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, which phases down climate-warming HFCs used in cooling, marked its 10th anniversary on October 15, 2026.
facts: Adopted at Kigali on October 15, 2016; entered into force in January 2019.
Aim: phase down HFCs; could avoid about 0.3–0.5°C of warming by 2100.
HFCs don't harm the ozone layer but warm hundreds or thousands of times more than CO2.
Called 'phase-down', not phase-out, because limited HFC use can continue.
India ratified in 2021: freeze by 2028, 10% cut by 2032, 85% cut by 2047.
Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs; nearly 99% of controlled ozone-depleting substances eliminated.
u0526.hook: India's Kigali ladder: 2028 freeze → 2032 cut 10% → 2047 cut 85%.
u0526.trap: Montreal Protocol (1987) = ozone-depleting substances like CFCs (phase-out); Kigali Amendment (2016) = HFCs (phase-down).

mcq.q: Under its Kigali Amendment commitments, by which year must India achieve an 85% reduction in HFCs?
mcq.why: India: freeze in 2028, 10% cut by 2032 and 85% reduction by 2047.

mcq.q: Which countries proposed in 2009 bringing HFCs under the Montreal Protocol, leading to the Kigali Amendment?
mcq.why: The Federated States of Micronesia and Mauritius made the proposal in 2009.

u0527.gist: On 30 September 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Green Energy Corridor Phase III to strengthen state transmission networks and add battery storage for renewable power.
facts: Approved by the Union Cabinet on 30 September 2026; target completion FY 2032–33.
Strengthens the Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) within States and Union Territories.
Supports evacuation of up to 135 GW renewable energy and 50 GWh battery storage (BESS).
Total outlay ₹1,86,405 crore: InSTS ₹1,36,378 crore; battery storage ₹50,000 crore.
Central Financial Support ₹54,082 crore, to lower intra-state transmission charges.
Supports India's target of 900 GW non-fossil installed capacity by 2035.
u0527.hook: Green Energy Corridor = a highway of power lines carrying green electricity from plants to the grid.
u0527.trap: 135 GW = renewable power to be evacuated; 50 GWh = battery storage to be deployed.
u0527.check: Components ₹1,36,378 crore + ₹50,000 crore = ₹1,86,378 crore, not the stated total ₹1,86,405 crore.

mcq.q: Green Energy Corridor Phase III, approved in September 2026, aims to deploy how much Battery Energy Storage System capacity by FY 2032–33?
mcq.why: It targets 50 GWh of BESS plus evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewables.

mcq.q: Which transmission network does Green Energy Corridor Phase III (2026) mainly strengthen?
mcq.why: Phase III strengthens the Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) within States and UTs.

u0528.gist: On World Ozone Day (16 September 2026), MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh launched India's Net Zero Portal and NAPCC Dashboard in Mumbai for transparent climate action.
facts: Launched 16 September 2026 in Mumbai by MoS Environment Kirti Vardhan Singh, on World Ozone Day.
Net Zero Portal: voluntary registration and disclosure of Net Zero commitments by Indian entities.
NAPCC Dashboard: single view of progress of National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
NDC for 2031–2035 (submitted 24 April 2026): 47% intensity cut, about 60% non-fossil capacity by 2035.
Early wins: 40% non-fossil target met in 2021, nine years early; 50% met June 2025.
Emissions intensity fell 37.38% by 2022 vs 2005; non-fossil about 55% of capacity (30 September 2026).
u0528.hook: Target ladders for 2015 → 2022 → 2026: non-fossil share 40 → 50 → 60%; intensity cut 33–35 → 45 → 47%.
u0528.trap: The 2015 INDC and 2022 update targets are 'by 2030'; the 2026 NDC targets are 'by 2035'.

mcq.q: In which city were India's Net Zero Portal and the NAPCC Dashboard launched on World Ozone Day 2026?
mcq.why: MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh launched them in Mumbai on 16 September 2026.

mcq.q: Under India's NDC for 2031–2035, submitted in April 2026, what share of installed power capacity should be non-fossil by 2035?
mcq.why: The 2026 NDC raised the non-fossil target to about 60% by 2035.

u0529.gist: The fifth Swachh Sagar, Surakshit Sagar drive (12–19 September 2026), led by the Earth Sciences Ministry, rallied citizens for coastal cleanup and ocean care.
facts: Fifth edition held 12 to 19 September 2026; launched on 1 September.
Meaning: Clean Coast, Safe Sea; led by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
Beach cleanups planned at 100-plus locations, with human chains, cycling rallies and marathons.
Included what MoES called the first national Ocean Olympiad for students and youth.
Campaign began on 5 July 2022; goals: consume responsibly, segregate waste at home, dispose responsibly.
u0529.hook: Three goals follow an item's life: Consume → Segregate → Dispose (all responsibly).
u0529.trap: The campaign started in 2022; the 2026 drive is its fifth edition.

mcq.q: Which ministry leads the 'Swachh Sagar, Surakshit Sagar' campaign, whose fifth edition was held in September 2026?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
mcq.why: The campaign is led by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).

u0530.gist: Project Great Indian Bustard added three chicks, taking fourth-year captive hatchings to 26 and the captive stock to 94 birds (14 June 2026).
facts: Announced by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on 14 June 2026.
Fourth breeding year: 26 chicks; 18 by artificial insemination, four natural, four from wild eggs.
Captive stock has grown to 94 birds.
Three chicks hatched in the wild in Rajasthan through a 'jumpstart' intervention.
Project launched by Rajasthan's Chief Minister on 5 June 2013, first in Desert National Park, Jaisalmer.
GIB (Godawan; Ardeotis nigriceps): Critically Endangered state bird of Rajasthan; grassland health indicator.
u0530.trap: 26 = chicks hatched in the fourth year; 94 = total captive stock.

mcq.q: As of June 2026, how many birds were in the captive stock of Project Great Indian Bustard?
mcq.why: Captive stock grew to 94 birds; 26 chicks hatched in the fourth year.

mcq.q: Project Great Indian Bustard, launched by Rajasthan on 5 June 2013, began in which protected area?
mcq.why: It began initially in the Desert National Park (DNP), Jaisalmer.

u0531.gist: Bhupender Yadav inaugurated WWF's Global Conservation Conference in Jaipur on 21 September 2026, where growth in India's conservation networks was highlighted.
facts: Inaugurated by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav at Jaipur on 21 September 2026.
Protected areas: around 750 earlier → more than 1,000 now.
Tiger reserves: 47 → 58; elephant reserves: 30 → 33.
Ramsar sites: 24 → 103.
WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature): independent body formed in 1961, based in Switzerland.
u0531.trap: 58 = tiger reserves; 33 = elephant reserves; 103 = Ramsar sites. Don't mix them.

mcq.q: At the WWF Global Conservation Conference in Jaipur (September 2026), how many tiger reserves did India cite?
mcq.why: Tiger reserves rose from 47 earlier to 58 as cited in 2026.

u0532.gist: The Union Cabinet approved the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana to add 5,000 MW of floating solar with storage, generating power without using scarce land.
facts: PM-SSY pairs Floating Solar PV (FSPV) projects with co-located Energy Storage Systems (ESS).
Target: add 5,000 MW of floating-solar capacity across all States and UTs.
Aid: ₹1 crore per MW after commissioning; up to ₹50 lakh per feasibility study.
Floating-solar potential about 102.18 GWp (NISE); only about 700 MW operational at approval.
Expected: cut about 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year; 16,000–17,000 jobs.
Solar capacity rose over 58 times: 2.82 GW (March 2014) → 164.59 GW (31 July 2026).
u0532.hook: Surya (sun) + Sarovar (lake) = solar panels floating on lakes and reservoirs.
u0532.trap: ALMM-enlisted module capacity crossed 200 GW (August 2026), but actual module manufacturing capacity was about 192 GW (June 2026); the source says they differ.

mcq.q: How much floating-solar capacity does the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (2026) seek to add?
mcq.why: PM-SSY seeks to add 5,000 MW of floating solar across all States and UTs.

mcq.q: What Central Financial Assistance will eligible projects get under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana after commissioning?
mcq.why: CFA is ₹1 crore per MW; feasibility studies may get up to ₹50 lakh per project.

u0533.gist: India launched its first Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems on August 17, 2026, at UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
facts: Launched August 17, 2026 at an official side event of UNCCD COP17, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
Under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; published by ATREE.
Aims to stop grasslands, scrublands and ravines being wrongly called 'wastelands'.
Covers Himalayan and Terai grasslands, Thar and Banni, Deccan savannas, ravines, coastal and desert landscapes.
UNCCD COP17 ran 17–28 August 2026; theme 'Restoring Land, Restoring Hope'.
2026 = International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (UNGA Resolution 76/253, 15 March 2022); FAO leads.
u0533.hook: ONEs = Open Natural Ecosystems: grasslands are 'ONEs', not wastelands.
u0533.trap: The Guide was launched at UNCCD COP17 (desertification convention), not at a UNFCCC climate COP.

mcq.q: Where was India's first Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems launched in August 2026?
mcq.why: It was launched at a side event of UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

mcq.q: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 2026 as the International Year of what?
mcq.why: Resolution 76/253 proclaimed 2026 the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.

u0534.gist: On 15 July 2026, the Supreme Court conditionally allowed Uttar Pradesh to go ahead with the Kukrail Night Safari and Zoological Park in Lucknow.
facts: Supreme Court permission (15 July 2026) is conditional, not a blanket environmental clearance.
Site: inside the 2,027-hectare Kukrail Reserve Forest, on Lucknow's outskirts.
Kukrail has UP's first gharial rehabilitation centre, set up in 1975.
Project cost ₹1,510 crore; spread over 855 acres.
Phase I: Night Safari and Eco-tourism Zone; Phase II: Day Zoo.
Billed as India's first dedicated urban night safari.
u0534.hook: Kukrail forest: 2,027 hectares, read it like the year 2027.
u0534.trap: 2,027 hectares = whole reserve forest; 855 acres = project area (different units too).

mcq.q: The Kukrail Night Safari and Zoological Park, conditionally allowed by the Supreme Court in July 2026, is in which city?
mcq.why: The project is in the Kukrail Reserve Forest on the outskirts of Lucknow.

mcq.q: Kukrail Reserve Forest in Lucknow houses Uttar Pradesh's first rehabilitation centre, set up in 1975, for which animal?
mcq.why: It is home to UP's first gharial rehabilitation centre, established in 1975.

u0535.gist: Union Minister Prataprao Jadhav opened Prakriti Café, a workplace food outlet based on Ayush Ahaar, at Ayush Bhawan, New Delhi, on 22 July 2026.
facts: Inaugurated by Union Minister Prataprao Jadhav on 22 July 2026.
Located at Ayush Bhawan, New Delhi.
A workplace food outlet that brings Ayush Ahaar principles into daily meals.
Promotes mindful eating and nutritious diets rooted in India's traditional knowledge.

mcq.q: Prakriti Café, inaugurated at Ayush Bhawan, New Delhi in July 2026, is based on which initiative's principles?
mcq.why: The café offers food inspired by the Ayush Ahaar initiative.

u0536.gist: India's Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme reached 20% blending in 2025, cutting crude dependence, supporting farmers and lowering road transport emissions.
facts: E20 = 20% ethanol + 80% petrol; India first achieved 20% blending in 2025.
Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) runs 1 November to 31 October, since November 2023.
EBP launched 2003; 2018 Biofuels Policy aimed E20 by 2030; 2022 amendment advanced it to ESY 2025–26.
E10 achieved in June 2022; phased E20 rollout began 6 February 2023.
Capacity grew from 421 crore litres (2014) to about 2,000 crore litres (2026).
Gains since ESY 2014–15: forex savings over ₹1.97 lakh crore; farmer payments over ₹1.66 lakh crore.
u0536.trap: E85 is not 85% ethanol: in the US it contains about 51–83%, for flex-fuel vehicles.

mcq.q: The 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels advanced India's E20 target to which Ethanol Supply Year?
mcq.why: The 2018 policy aimed at E20 by 2030; the 2022 amendment advanced it to ESY 2025–26.

mcq.q: Since November 2023, what period does India's Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) cover?
mcq.why: Since November 2023, the ESY runs from 1 November to 31 October.

u0537.gist: Tamil Nadu began placing 3D-printed artificial reef modules off Rameswaram under PMMSY to restore fish habitats and support coastal communities.
facts: Off Rameswaram, Ramanathapuram district; Phase II of Tamil Nadu's artificial-reef programme.
Supported under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).
Each module weighs about 1 tonne; made by Chennai startup Tvasta (IIT Madras-incubated).
Partner: Visakhapatnam Regional Centre of ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute; led by Dr Joe K. Kizhakudan.
Complex shapes with crevices and folds, unlike reinforced-concrete reefs.
Funded by Centre and State in a 60:40 ratio.
u0537.hook: Matsya = fish: PMMSY money builds new homes (reefs) for fish.
u0537.trap: Startup Tvasta is Chennai-based; the partner CMFRI centre is in Visakhapatnam.

mcq.q: Off which coastal town has Tamil Nadu begun deploying 3D-printed artificial reef modules under PMMSY in 2026?
mcq.why: The modules are being deployed off Rameswaram in Ramanathapuram district.

u0538.gist: SDSN's Sustainable Development Report 2026 ranks India 94th of 169 countries (score 68.3), up 18 places since 2015, but still off track for 2030.
facts: Released by SDSN on June 23, 2026; India 94th of 169, score 68.3 out of 100.
India rose 18 places, from 112th (2015) to 94th (2026); China improved 14 places.
Of 75 indicators: 25 on track, eight moderately improving, 33 stagnating, nine decreasing.
SDG 2: only cereal yield (3.6 t/ha, 2023) on track; stunting fell 37.9% → 35.5%.
Child wasting rose 16.9% (2017) → 18.7% (2020); adult obesity 4.91% → 7.27%.
Globally none of 17 SDGs is fully on course; 2025 was 1.43°C above pre-industrial.
u0538.trap: 169 appears twice: countries ranked and total SDG targets. India's trend shares use 75 indicators, not 169 targets.

mcq.q: What was India's rank in the Sustainable Development Report 2026 released by SDSN in June 2026?
mcq.why: India ranked 94th among 169 countries with a score of 68.3.

mcq.q: Per the Sustainable Development Report 2026, which is India's only SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) indicator on track?
mcq.why: Only cereal yield, 3.6 tonnes per hectare in 2023, is on track under SDG 2.
